metadata.title: THE ROLE OF SUBNATIONAL GOVERNMENTS IN ADULT SKILLS SYSTEMS: BELGIUM

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a policy/governance description of Belgium’s adult skills system and does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) or any assessment dataset with sampling weights. As a result, there is no complex survey design, plausible values framework, or replicate-weight scheme to apply. The tables present governance responsibilities and expenditure shares at subnational levels rather than model-based estimates from a weighted student sample. For this type of document, weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT/BRR) are not relevant because no survey-based statistical inference is conducted.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because the document does not use any cognitive assessment microdata with PV-based achievement scores (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC). The note is descriptive and institutional/governance-focused, summarizing responsibilities and expenditure allocations rather than estimating predictive models from test-item responses. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no analytic dataset with item-level missingness or imputation/deletion procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a qualitative/policy compilation approach to describe Belgium’s adult skills governance structure; no student-level analytic sample is constructed or reported.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Belgium country note provides an overview of how adult skills systems are governed across Belgium’s federal, regional, community, and local levels. It summarizes the allocation of responsibilities across policy areas (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) for adult education and training, vocational education and training, higher vocational education and training, continuous education and training, and active labour market policies. The document also describes key stakeholders (ministries, national employment office, expert councils, social partners, and regional public employment services) and how responsibilities differ between Flanders, Wallonia, Brussels, and the German-speaking community. Rather than reporting assessment performance, it uses governance/expenditure shares and institutional mapping to characterize decentralisation and coordination mechanisms. No student assessment data, sampling design, scaling, or PV-based benchmarks are used, so there are no psychometric or ML evaluation metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical OECD policy country note that does not conduct an ILSA-style student-level analysis. Consequently, there is no assessment cycle, grade/domain, analytic sample size, PV handling, missing-data strategy, or ML model evaluation to extract. The extraction is therefore intentionally sparse on data-analytic fields, while governance responsibilities and expenditure allocation are documented descriptively.
